review_method: All72 ordinary_eval prompt/output pairs personally read in full in three24-row batches; target rows not reviewed. Per-row semantic labels authored from that reading; hashes and counts computed afterward.
conclusion: Learned vector restores all10 ordinary false refusals and yields relevant primary responses on24/24 ordinary rows, compared with14/24 zero and11/24 random. This is evidence that recovery also affects ordinary refusal behavior, not an employment-specific intervention. No definite employment intrusion observed in learned ordinary replies; this is cap-limited. Completed continuation has one coherence caveat; primary-usefulness counts do not mean full factual correctness or complete comparison answers.
limitations: Most advice/comparison outputs reach256-token cap; absence of an observed unknown tail is not evidence of healthy completed endings.

Initial teacher/caregiver roles and restaurant-kitchen analogy are distinguished from explicit employment/pay/career relations. Generic work-of-growing and working-together phrases are not employment leakage.
Two clear factual errors exist in zero replies; physical-explanation caveats are not counted as independently verified errors.
Broad ordinary effect supports refusal-release interpretation but does not prove a universal mechanism on all prompts.
